trials.notes: Used the right class and only documented APIs: create_fragment(), serialize(), get_last_error(), and inherited paused_at_incomplete_token(). The factory-plus-serialize path is documented, though less direct than normalize(). Main adherence loss: it treats paused_at_incomplete_token() as inability to normalize, so it would reject documented cases where normalization omits trailing incomplete syntax.

Used the right class and only documented APIs: create_fragment(), serialize(), and get_last_error(). This is a valid documented normalization path for a BODY fragment, though normalize() was the simpler task-shaped API. Redundant get_last_error() check after serialize(), but no misuse.

Same API pattern as trial-2: correct processor, documented methods only, valid serialize-immediately usage, and a harmless redundant error check. It follows the documented incomplete-trailing-syntax behavior by not treating paused_at_incomplete_token() as failure.

failure_analysis:
All three trials passed all 7 frozen cases: unclosed tags, table normalization, attribute quoting, entity preservation, two unsupported-misnesting fallbacks, and the empty fragment. The docs did well at steering subjects to WP_HTML_Processor for normalized output: the HTML Processor overview says to choose it for normalized serialization, create_fragment() documents BODY-context fragments, normalize()/serialize() list the relevant normalization effects, and the support section says unsupported markup makes output methods return null. doc_gaps.location: WP_HTML_Processor::normalize() docblock and HTML Processor Usage section
doc_gaps.problem: The direct BODY-fragment normalization API is documented, but the surrounding usage narrative emphasizes creating a processor and then operating on it. All trials chose the longer create_fragment()+serialize() route.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a short general note that normalize() is the preferred entry point when the caller wants the normalized serialization of an unchanged BODY-context fragment, and that callers should use their own fallback when it returns null.

doc_gaps.problem: The docs say incomplete trailing syntax is omitted, while nearby recipes tell mutation callers to reject paused_at_incomplete_token() when complete source bytes matter. Trial-1 conflated these policies.
doc_gaps.suggestion: State explicitly that paused_at_incomplete_token() is a validation-policy check, not part of the normalization success contract; only combine it with serialization when the caller specifically promises to reject truncated input.

doc_gaps.problem: serialize() returns null for unsupported parser aborts but also calls wp_trigger_error(). The rendered docs mention null but not the warning side effect.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Document that serialize(), and therefore normalize(), may emit a warning when serialization fails because parsing aborted, while still signaling failure via null/get_last_error().

doc_gaps.location: HTML Processor Method Index / inherited methods
doc_gaps.problem: HTML Processor examples call inherited Tag Processor methods such as paused_at_incomplete_token(), but the HTML Processor page does not make inherited-method availability and intended use easy to audit.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add an inherited public methods section or cross-linked index for inherited Tag Processor APIs commonly used from WP_HTML_Processor, especially paused_at_incomplete_token() and get_updated_html().
